4732.name: USS Co., Ltd.
4732.japanese_name: 株式会社ユー・エス・エス
4732.description: USS operates used-vehicle auctions that match dealers and other members through physical sites and remote bidding. It earns consignment fees, contract-completion fees and successful-bid fees. Group businesses also purchase and sell used vehicles and recycle vehicles and industrial equipment.
4732.share_note: April 1, 2024 split, two shares for one. March 2022 and March 2023 EPS are divided by two and weighted-average shares multiplied by two. The March 2024 release already applies the split. Later current-year figures are already on this basis.

Bear: Illustrative. Lower auction throughput and weaker fee realization reduce revenue and margin. A lower multiple reflects weaker earnings durability.
Base: Illustrative. Moderate revenue growth and an attributable margin near recent results. Shares held at the selected annual weighted average. The multiple is an assumption.
Bull: Illustrative. Higher auction volume and better fee realization support margin. A higher assumed multiple tests greater confidence in fee earnings.

research_prompts.thesis: A dense auction network could support a durable fee business if listing volumes and completion rates hold as fees rise.
research_prompts.evidence: Compare vehicle consignments, successful contracts, completion rates and fee revenue with the issuer’s operating disclosures. Check whether annual cash flow supports reported profit.
research_prompts.catalysts: Track auction volumes and the impact of fee changes on both sides of the marketplace.
research_prompts.risks: A tighter used-vehicle supply or dealer migration could reduce throughput. Recycling and vehicle resale add exposure to prices and mix.
research_prompts.invalidation: Sustained declines in consignments and completion rates following fee increases, coupled with weaker operating margins, would weaken the network-pricing thesis.

3064.name: MonotaRO Co., Ltd.
3064.description: MonotaRO sells indirect materials online to businesses in manufacturing, construction and vehicle maintenance. Its assortment includes private-label and imported products. A broad catalog, inventory availability and tailored recommendations support repeat purchasing.
3064.share_note: April 1, 2021 split, two shares for one. The December 2021 release already reflects the split in EPS and weighted-average shares. Later current-year figures are carried on the same basis.

Bear: Illustrative. Slower order growth and higher fulfillment costs pressure the attributable margin. The multiple is lower to test weaker growth durability.
Base: Illustrative. Continued order growth with an attributable margin near recent results. Shares held at the selected annual weighted average. The multiple is an assumption.
Bull: Illustrative. Faster sales growth and better fulfillment efficiency lift attributable margin. A higher multiple tests greater confidence in those gains.

research_prompts.thesis: Broad product availability and convenient repeat ordering could support growth, with fulfillment scale helping preserve incremental profitability.
research_prompts.evidence: Compare sales growth, operating margins and cash conversion. Follow issuer disclosures on repeat customers and enterprise procurement adoption.
research_prompts.catalysts: Monitor enterprise customer connections, order growth and distribution-center utilization.
research_prompts.risks: Higher delivery or labor costs, weak customer retention, or prolonged investment in fulfillment could reduce cash conversion.
research_prompts.invalidation: A persistent slowdown in sales and repeat purchasing alongside declining margins and cash flow after capital expenditure would weaken the scale thesis.
